title: History 7: Latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion (2022)

questions.q: Why does the latent diffusion paper run diffusion in an autoencoder's latent space?
options: A pixel-space network is evaluated on all pixels, though most bits of an image describe imperceptible detail
Diffusion cannot be trained on images with three channels
It makes sampling a single step
questions.answer: A pixel-space network is evaluated on all pixels, though most bits of an image describe imperceptible detail
questions.why: Figure 2 of the paper: "Most bits of a digital image correspond to imperceptible details", yet the backbone must still be evaluated on all pixels. The first stage removes that detail, and the diffusion model handles the semantic composition.

questions.q: In the lab, from the 512×512 pixel grid to the 64×64 latent grid, how much does the self-attention matrix shrink?
options: A factor of 4096, because positions fall by 64 and the matrix is positions squared
questions.answer: A factor of 4096, because positions fall by 64 and the matrix is positions squared
questions.why: The ratio row prints 262,144 against 4,096 positions, and 68,719,476,736 against 16,777,216 matrix entries. The convolution shrinks 64 times and the number of values 48 times.

questions.q: In the lab, what happens to the cost of the latent attention layer when the image side doubles from 512 to 1024?
questions.why: Positions go from 4,096 to 16,384, which is four times as many, and the attention cost goes with their square: 21.5 to 343.6 GFLOPs. The convolution grows only 4.00 times.

questions.q: The paper compares the pixel-space LDM-1 with LDM-4. What speed-up in training throughput does it report?
options: About 2.9 times, from 0.11 to 0.32 samples per second
None, the two train at the same speed
questions.answer: About 2.9 times, from 0.11 to 0.32 samples per second
questions.why: Table 6 of the paper, measured on its inpainting setup. Sampling is 3.7 times faster at 256 and 4.9 times at 512. Per-layer arithmetic like the lab's does not predict an end-to-end number.

questions.q: What does ComfyUI's CheckpointLoaderSimple return, and which parts of latent diffusion do they correspond to?
options: MODEL, CLIP and VAE: the denoising U-Net, the text encoder and the autoencoder
questions.answer: MODEL, CLIP and VAE: the denoising U-Net, the text encoder and the autoencoder
questions.why: RETURN_TYPES is ("MODEL", "CLIP", "VAE"), with tooltips naming the model for denoising latents, the CLIP model for encoding prompts, and the VAE for moving between pixels and latent space.

questions.q: When did Stability AI announce the public release of Stable Diffusion, and under what licence?
questions.why: Stability AI's page is dated Aug 22 and says the model is released under a Creative ML OpenRAIL-M licence; the Hugging Face post of the same day is dated 22 August 2022. The latent diffusion paper itself was posted on 20 December 2021.
